      Your character. Pick one to sit beside your name on the board. More appear as your badges add up.

      Frames. A ring round your character, which everyone sees beside your name on the board. Some come as the class fills the jar. The blazing ones come from long streaks and the top of the levels.

      Colours. Unlock a new look for the jugs, scales and rulers as your badges add up. The last fourteen are different: nobody earns them alone. They arrive for the whole class as the jar is filled again and again.

      Badge colours. The hardest to get. Each one comes with one of the toughest badges, and each changes the whole screen. Dragon Hoard is legendary: it needs Stretch 6 in every game.

      Seasonal colours. Only here for part of the year, and some years two overlap. Party arrives for the whole class when you beat your teacher's class challenge.

      Backgrounds. One more to choose from every time the class fills the jar. They sit behind everything, so the jugs and the numbers stay exactly as easy to read.

      Turn off if this iPad feels slow. The colours and backgrounds stay, they just stand still.

      Flames. The colour of the flames that build as your streak grows. Keep a streak going to light the next colour.

      Trails. A sparkle left behind the handle while you drag on Set it yourself questions.

        Change what the class jar is worth

        These live in your Google Sheet, not in this file, so setting them here sets them for every laptop in the room. Each one picks the change up within about half a minute. You can also type straight into the Class goal tab of the sheet.

        Every correct answer is worth the same, whatever level you are on. Three right in a row doubles your points, and six in a row triples them. One wrong answer sends the streak back to zero.

          Turn on one shared board for every device

          Right now each device keeps its own board. To pool every laptop and iPad into class leaderboards, the game needs a Google Sheet of your own to write to. It takes about ten minutes.

          1. Make a new Google Sheet, then choose Extensions → Apps Script.
          2. Paste the leaderboard script (the .gs file that came with this game) into Code.gs, replacing what is there.
          3. Add an HTML file named exactly Page (the + beside Files) and paste this whole game file into it.
          4. Choose Deploy → New deployment → Web app. Execute as Me, who has access Anyone. The address it gives you, ending /exec, is the link children open.
          5. Add one tab to the sheet for each class, named for its class code (for example 5Semmler). Children type that code before their name, so make codes hard to guess.
          6. Reopen the sheet. In the new Measuring Lab menu choose Set teacher name and password. To use the teacher buttons, type that name on the game's name screen and then the password.
